sections.vendors: M&S published its Plan A ESG Report 2026, confirming 100% of clothing cotton is now from more responsible sources (BCI, organic, or recycled). The RE:Spark programme was launched to support fashion supply chain decarbonisation, focusing on helping key manufacturing partners transition to renewable energy.
sections.sustainability: M&S is on track to replace all virgin polyester with recycled polyester by end of 2026 — a landmark commitment for the brand's owned label clothing. Plan A 2026 shows 100% of textiles in fashion and home from preferred alternatives (excluding trims). Scope 1 and 2 emissions have fallen 38% vs the 2016/17 baseline.
sections.sourcing: M&S sources from India, Sri Lanka, Turkey, Bangladesh, and China. Key strategic suppliers include Shahi Exports, Arvind Mills, Brandix Lanka, MAS Holdings, and Eastman Exports. The brand is deepening its long-term strategic partnerships rather than expanding its supplier base.
sections.strategy: M&S made its London Fashion Week debut in 2026, signalling elevated brand positioning ambitions. The brand is investing in premium own-label ranges (Autograph, Per Una) alongside its everyday value staples. Store transformation programme continues with enhanced clothing departments.
sections.pricing: M&S has successfully repositioned on price quality perception, with clothing seen as offering strong value for quality at its price points. The brand has benefited from trade-down from premium brands and trade-up from supermarket clothing — occupying a sweet spot in the market.
sections.launches: M&S AW2026 collections featured heavily recycled polyester outerwear and knitwear, with Autograph debuting GOTS organic cotton lines. The brand launched a kids' clothing expansion with enhanced sustainable material content across school wear.
sections.gossip: M&S's London Fashion Week debut was met with mixed industry reaction — some observers praised its ambition, others questioned the brand's credibility in a fashion-week context versus its traditional positioning. The RE:Spark supply chain programme is seen as one of the most substantive decarbonisation initiatives by a UK retailer.
soWhat: Virgin polyester replacement with recycled by end 2026 is a hard deadline — any M&S supplier still supplying virgin polyester fabrics must immediately transition to GRS-certified recycled alternatives or risk contract termination

RE:Spark renewable energy programme means M&S will actively support suppliers in solar/renewable transitions — strategic suppliers in India and Sri Lanka should engage with RE:Spark now to access potential co-investment support

100% responsible cotton sourced opens the question of certification mix (BCI vs GOTS vs recycled) — suppliers offering GOTS organic or recycled cotton can differentiate themselves above the baseline BCI minimum
